cases.quote: EN: A third order opportunity exists for inter-character spacing expansion, to take up to a maximum of a quarter em space, with respect to the corresponding character size, between two consecutive inseparable characters (cl-08) which are of different kinds. — JA: 後ろに配置する分離禁止文字（cl-08）の文字が，前に配置する分離禁止文字（cl-08）とは別の種類の文字の場合，優先順位が第3段階の最大で四分アキまで文字サイズ比で均等に空ける処理は可とする．
cases.rationale: §A.27 lists U+2014 EM DASH too, under the Remark `proportionally-spaced`, so the declared frame is what decides which of the two appendix rows describes this occurrence — `full-em` is the frame that reaches cl-08 rather than cl-27, and `A.8/em-dash/ideographic-frame`'s own case is where this project first established that the ideographic frame, not the code point alone, is what puts an em dash in cl-08 at all. Both occurrences here declare it, so the pair sits at the coordinate §E.2 note 4 is actually about, cl-08 against cl-08, rather than resolving to §A.27's proportional cl-27 instead. The answer is `none` because an identical character is certainly of its own kind under every reading of 種類 this workspace has considered: `docs/decisions/inseparable-character-kind.md`'s own grid answers `same` at this em-dash diagonal cell under all three candidate readings alike, R1, R2 and R3 included — R3, the one reading its own "Why" section refutes outright rather than merely disfavors, is refuted elsewhere in that same grid, at the three kunojiten diagonal cells (〳,〳), (〴,〴) and (〵,〵), where it calls each mark "of a different kind" from itself, not at this em-dash cell, where it agrees with R1 and R2. This cell is consequently not one the adopted reading (R2, mark family) decides differently from the rejected member-identity reading (R1); both answer "same kind" here, so `Expansion::None` follows under either, and this case's own point is that identity — not the choice between R1 and R2 — is what settles it.

cases.quote: EN: A third order opportunity exists for inter-character spacing expansion, to take up to a maximum of a quarter em space, with respect to the corresponding character size, between two consecutive inseparable characters (cl-08) which are of different kinds. — JA: 後ろに配置する分離禁止文字（cl-08）の文字が，前に配置する分離禁止文字（cl-08）とは別の種類の文字の場合，優先順位が第3段階の最大で四分アキまで文字サイズ比で均等に空ける処理は可とする．
cases.rationale: The note's own words state the ceiling directly: "up to a maximum of a quarter em space" — one quarter of JLReq's own em, which this project's own unit of measure fixes at 720 (ADR 0007), so a quarter em is 180 units, `em(180)` in `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table6.rs`'s own `(8, 8)` cell. The note also names its own priority directly — "a third order opportunity", §E.1's third stage — which is the `stage: 3` this case asserts alongside the ceiling. `spaces` is empty because Table 1's own cl-08-against-cl-08 cell is blank (`spec/captured/table1.en.tsv`), carrying no conditional space of either referent's at all: this note's whole opportunity rides on Table 6 alone, at a coordinate Table 1 says nothing about, which is exactly why the coordinate was unreachable before ADR-0021 moved Table 6's opportunity off `ConditionalSpace` (the carrier `spaces_of` only ever populates from an existing Table 1 term) and onto `Boundary::expansion`, read independent of Table 1's own terms. This case and `E.2/two-em-dashes/an-identical-inseparable-character-is-not-a-different-kind` differ in exactly one character of `text` — the second em dash replaced by a horizontal ellipsis — which is the whole of the contrast §E.2 note 4 draws: the same coordinate, cl-08 against cl-08, answered oppositely because the two occurrences are visibly different marks rather than the same one, and `docs/decisions/inseparable-character-kind.md`'s own grid answers "different" at this off-diagonal, cross-family cell under every one of its three candidate readings alike.

permitted.source: JLReq §E.2 note 4's own worked contrast — two visibly different inseparable characters

forbidden.why: An identical mark on both sides of the boundary is one thing and two visibly different marks are the note's own named contrast; answering `none` here treats every cl-08 pair alike regardless of whether the two occurrences share a kind, and it misses the whole point of the note's own condition — that a *different*-kind pair is exactly the one this note opens an opportunity for.

cases.quote: EN: A third order opportunity exists for inter-character spacing expansion between a preceding Western character (cl-27) and a trailing postfixed abbreviation (cl-13), unless the preceding Western character (cl-27) is used as a symbol of a quantity or a European numeral, in which case no inter-character spacing expansion is allowed between them. — JA: 前に配置する欧文用文字（cl-27）と後ろに配置する後置省略記号（cl-13）の字間は，空ける調整が可能な箇所である（優先順位は第3段階）．しかし，前に配置する欧文用文字（cl-27）が量を示す記号（量記号）又はアラビア数字の場合は，空ける調整箇所としてはならない．
cases.rationale: The note's own general rule, unqualified by either of its two named exceptions: the preceding occurrence, `A`, carries no declared `role` and its own Appendix A key is not one of the ten European numerals §A.19, §A.24 and §A.27 all enumerate (`docs/decisions/european-numeral-by-code-point.md`, which `C.2/western-character-then-postfixed-abbreviation/an-ordinary-western-character-permits-a-break`'s own rationale already cites for this identical fixture). Neither "used as a symbol of a quantity" nor "a European numeral" is triggered, so the third order opportunity the note's own general rule states stands: a quarter em ceiling at the third priority stage, read from Table 6's own `(27, 13)` cell (`em(180)`, `stage: 3`, citing this note), independent of Table 1's own blank cell at the identical coordinate — the same reachability ADR-0021 gives every coordinate this file's cases publish. This input is byte-identical to `C.2/western-character-then-postfixed-abbreviation/an-ordinary-western-character-permits-a-break`'s own, the breakability sibling of this expansion case at the same coordinate.

cases.quote: EN: A third order opportunity exists for inter-character spacing expansion between a preceding Western character (cl-27) and a trailing postfixed abbreviation (cl-13), unless the preceding Western character (cl-27) is used as a symbol of a quantity or a European numeral, in which case no inter-character spacing expansion is allowed between them. — JA: 前に配置する欧文用文字（cl-27）と後ろに配置する後置省略記号（cl-13）の字間は，空ける調整が可能な箇所である（優先順位は第3段階）．しかし，前に配置する欧文用文字（cl-27）が量を示す記号（量記号）又はアラビア数字の場合は，空ける調整箇所としてはならない．
cases.rationale: §C.2 note 11 and §E.2 note 10 state the identical exception in the identical six words — "used as a symbol of a quantity or a European numeral" — over the identical ordered class pair, cl-27 before cl-13; one note asks whether a line may break there and the other asks whether the boundary may be expanded, but the condition that withdraws the opportunity is the same sentence read twice. `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/evaluate.rs`'s own `note_governed_expansion` reads that condition through `quantity_or_numeral`, the identical function §C.2 note 11's own `note_governed_refusal` already reads at this coordinate, rather than a second, independently-drifting copy of the phrase. This case and `E.2/western-character-then-postfixed-abbreviation/the-general-rule-opens-a-third-stage-quarter-em` are consequently the expansion-side twin of `C.2/quantity-symbol-then-postfixed-abbreviation/a-declared-role-forbids-a-break` and `C.2/western-character-then-postfixed-abbreviation/an-ordinary-western-character-permits-a-break`: the same input, `Role::QuantitySymbol` declared on the preceding item, differing from the general-rule case in exactly the one declared field that changes the answer — the same minimal-difference shape the C.2 pair already uses — only the question this pair asks is expansion rather than breakability. The declared role withdraws the note's own opportunity outright, `Expansion::None`, rather than narrowing its stated quarter em, because the note's own text states the exception as excluding the boundary from the third order opportunity entirely. The expectation now also asserts `rule: "E.2#10"` beside `kind: "none"`, a strengthening warranted by the specification rather than a correction made to match code: `note_governed_expansion`'s own doc (`crates/jlreq-spacing/src/evaluate.rs`, ~line 904) states directly that the `rule` half of its returned pair is "the note that states the condition being checked" and never Table 6's own bare §E citation, because a withdrawn opportunity at this coordinate is still a fact §E.2 note 10 states — its one sentence gives both the opportunity and its own exception in one breath — and the code names that literal choice as `RuleId::E_2_NOTE_10` for `(27, 13)` exactly as it names `RuleId::E_2_NOTE_4` for the structurally identical `(8, 8)` withdrawal the unit test `expansion_rule_still_names_the_governing_note_when_it_withdraws_the_opportunity` (`crates/jlreq-spacing/src/evaluate.rs`, ~line 2030) exercises directly. Table 6's own `(27, 13)` row corroborates the same citation independent of the note-governed branch: `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table6.rs`'s own cell at that coordinate carries `rule: RuleId::E_2_NOTE_10`, so the two readings agree by construction rather than by coincidence, the identical guarantee `expansion_rule_of`'s own doc states for both of its conditioned coordinates.

forbidden.why: The preceding item declares `Role::QuantitySymbol`, the note's own first named exception stated in the caller's own terms; publishing the general rule's quarter-em ceiling here ignores the declared role and answers as though no exception applied, the same failure `C.2/quantity-symbol-then-postfixed-abbreviation/a-declared-role-forbids-a-break`'s own `forbidden` entry names for the breakability question at the identical coordinate.

cases.quote: EN: There is no opportunity for inter-character spacing expansion between a preceding grouped numeral (cl-24) and a trailing postfixed abbreviation (cl-13), unless the alternative approach is chosen which allows a line to break between a preceding grouped numeral (cl-24) and the trailing PERCENT SIGN "%", where PERCENT SIGN "%" shall be treated as a member of the ideographic character (cl-19) class, in front of which inter-character spacing is expandable. — JA: 前に配置する連数字中の文字（cl-24）と後ろに配置する後置省略記号（cl-13）の字間は，空ける調整に使用できない．ただし，パーセント記号[％] (PERCENT SIGN)については，前に配置する連数字中の文字（cl-24）との字間で2行に分割することを許容する方法もある．この場合は，パーセント記号[％] (PERCENT SIGN)は，漢字等（cl-19）の文字クラスに含めるので，空ける調整が可能な箇所になる．
cases.rationale:
This input is byte-identical to `A.13/grouped-numeral-percent/line-break`'s own, the breakability sibling of this expansion case at the identical coordinate: a half-em `5` (§A.24 lists U+0035 with the Remark `half-width`, which is what makes the leading digit cl-24 rather than §A.19's unqualified full-width listing or §A.27's `proportionally-spaced` one) followed by the full-width percent sign, reached through the Appendix A preamble Note's own folding of U+FF05 onto the U+0025 key §A.13 lists with an empty Remarks cell (cl-13). §E.2 note 8's own main clause denies any expansion opportunity at this coordinate outright, and Table 6's own `(24, 13)` cell agrees: `limit: None`, citing this note (`crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table6.rs`). That is the whole of `permitted[0]`.

The note's own second clause states a genuine alternative — the percent sign, and only the percent sign, treated as a member of cl-19, 'in front of which inter-character spacing is expandable' — and Table 6's own `(24, 19)` cell backs that alternative with a real captured amount: a half em at the second priority stage, citing the generic §E opportunity (`limit: Some(em(360))`, `stage: 2`, `rule: OPPORTUNITIES_FOR_INTER_CHARACTER_SPACE_EXPANSION_DURING_LINE_ADJUSTMENT`, address `E`). That is the reading `A.13/percent-sign/kinsoku-loose-reclassification`'s own classify-side ladder already publishes for exactly this code point under `kinsoku.level: loose`, and this case was drafted to publish the parallel expansion rung beside it as a second, nested `permitted` entry — until checking whether this workspace can actually produce that answer found that it cannot, on any policy this workspace can construct, for two independent reasons. First, `crates/jlreq-class/src/classify.rs`'s own `RECLASSIFICATIONS` table (four rows: §C.2 note 1's `々`, note 2's cl-10, and note 3's two cl-11 rows) carries no percent-sign entry at all — `jlreq_class::classify` never answers cl-19 for U+FF05 under any policy today, which this project's own changelog already states plainly ('applies §C.2's three reclassification notes'; note 9's percent-sign alternative is not among the three §C.2 states and none stand in for it). Second, and independently of the first: even if it did, `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/evaluate.rs`'s own `class_of` — the function `Adjacency::before_position`/`after_position` call to resolve the class ordinals `expansion_of` and `expansion_rule_of` key their Table 6 lookup on — resolves every item's class under a hardcoded `Policy::JLREQ`, never the `policy` parameter `boundary()` itself receives, so no `Policy` a caller constructs can route a different class into this lookup regardless of what `jlreq_class` might someday answer. Confirmed directly rather than assumed: a scratch probe (`boundary(adjacency, Policy::MAGAZINE)` over this exact fixture, run and removed before commit) answers `expansion: Expansion::None`, `expansion_rule: Some(RuleId::E_2_NOTE_8)` — the identical answer `Policy::JLREQ` gives, never the `(24, 19)` cell's half em. Publishing a loose-level rung here would therefore not be describing a reading the format merely cannot yet select — `A.13/percent-sign/kinsoku-loose-reclassification`'s own already-published second and third rungs are exactly that kind of claim, unaudited by this round — it would be asserting an answer this workspace is now verified not to produce on any input, which ADR 0006 does not permit a case to do. `docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s own `E.2#8` entry records this as a scope limit rather than a silence.

permitted.source: JLReq §E.2 note 8's own main clause — the only reading this workspace can construct today

forbidden.why: The half-em, second-stage ceiling Table 6's own `(24, 19)` cell states, which is what a reader who takes §E.2 note 8's alternative clause at face value — and `A.13/percent-sign/kinsoku-loose-reclassification`'s own classify-side ladder alongside it — would expect a `kinsoku.level: loose` policy to produce here. This workspace verified the opposite directly (this case's own rationale): `jlreq_class::classify`'s `RECLASSIFICATIONS` table carries no percent-sign entry, and `jlreq_spacing::evaluate::class_of` resolves every item's class under a hardcoded `Policy::JLREQ` regardless of the policy `boundary()` itself receives, so no policy this workspace can construct ever reaches the `(24, 19)` cell from this coordinate. Publishing this reading as `permitted` would assert a path that does not exist.

cases.quote: EN: There is no opportunity for inter-character spacing expansion between a preceding grouped numeral (cl-24) and a trailing postfixed abbreviation (cl-13), unless the alternative approach is chosen which allows a line to break between a preceding grouped numeral (cl-24) and the trailing PERCENT SIGN "%", where PERCENT SIGN "%" shall be treated as a member of the ideographic character (cl-19) class, in front of which inter-character spacing is expandable. — JA: 前に配置する連数字中の文字（cl-24）と後ろに配置する後置省略記号（cl-13）の字間は，空ける調整に使用できない．ただし，パーセント記号[％] (PERCENT SIGN)については，前に配置する連数字中の文字（cl-24）との字間で2行に分割することを許容する方法もある．この場合は，パーセント記号[％] (PERCENT SIGN)は，漢字等（cl-19）の文字クラスに含めるので，空ける調整が可能な箇所になる．
cases.rationale:
Byte-identical to `A.13/grouped-numeral-degree-celsius/line-break`'s own input: the same half-em `5` (cl-24) followed by U+2103 DEGREE CELSIUS, a key §A.13 lists with an empty Remarks cell (cl-13) and no other Appendix A table names. §E.2 note 8's own alternative clause names PERCENT SIGN specifically, and no other member of cl-13 nor the class as a whole, so it never reaches this code point; Table 6's own `(24, 13)` cell applies unconditionally here exactly as it does for the digit-group case, `limit: None`, citing this note. No question in `spec/derived/questions.tsv` is addressed to `E.2#8` at all (checked directly: no row's `address` column reads `E.2#8`), so this coordinate has only the one reading `E.2/grouped-numeral-percent/the-main-clause-denies-expansion`'s own rationale already gives its sibling code point, and `standing` is `normative` for the identical reason.

The question this case exists to answer, and the reason it is not simply a duplicate of its sibling: `A.13/grouped-numeral-degree-celsius/line-break`, the breakability case at this identical coordinate, publishes a `kinsoku.level: very-loose` rung (`breakable: true`) beside its default, because §C.3's own Very loose (Newspapers) level lists 'Postfixed abbreviations (cl-13)' as a whole class (spec/snapshot/index.html, list item id612) — U+2103 is a member of cl-13, so Very loose relaxes it there exactly as it relaxes the percent sign. Does that same whole-class relaxation open an expansion opportunity too, the way §C.3's Loose level (which names the percent sign alone, id620) is read as putting §E.2 note 8's own reclassification in force for the percent sign in this file's sibling case? Read directly against §C.3's own words, no: the Very loose level's own sentence states 'Breaking a line is allowed before or after the following character classes even though Table 2 prohibits it' (id603), a form repeated with one added parenthetical — '(or characters)' — at the Loose (id613) and Strict (id621) levels alike, and replaced at Very strict by a different sentence entirely, 'Breaking a line is not allowed for any place where Table 2 prohibits it (no alternate rule explained in §C.2 Notes is applied.)' (id625), which declines §C.2's alternate rules rather than invoking one; no level's own sentence names a class change or a Table 6 coordinate at all — in contrast to §E.2 note 8's own alternative clause, which is the only sentence in the document that moves a cl-13 member into cl-19, and it names the percent sign alone rather than the class. Very loose's cl-13-as-a-whole-class permission is consequently orthogonal to what note 8's alternative states: it opens Table 2's door for every member of cl-13 including U+2103, but it touches no Table 6 coordinate at all, and even the percent sign's own reclassification is, per this case's sibling, unreachable in this workspace today regardless of what §C.3 states. So no policy this project's questions can construct changes this coordinate's expansion answer, and the differential the two A.13 breakability cases publish — a `very-loose` rung for the whole class beside a `loose` rung for the percent sign alone — has no expansion-side counterpart here: this is the scoping §E.2 note 8 itself draws, between one code point and a whole class, carried through to the one matrix (Table 6) whose own coordinate this note states directly.

permitted.source: JLReq §E.2 note 8's own main clause, unaffected by any level: the alternative clause never names this code point

forbidden.why: The half-em, second-stage ceiling `E.2/grouped-numeral-percent/the-main-clause-denies-expansion`'s own sibling coordinate would read under a reclassification to cl-19. §C.3's Very loose level relaxes cl-13 as a whole class for breakability, and a reader who conflates that whole-class permission with §E.2 note 8's own percent-sign-only reclassification might expect U+2103 to reach the identical `(24, 19)` cell under `kinsoku.level: very-loose`. Nothing in §C.3's own text does that: Very loose's own sentence names Table 2 alone, not a class change, and the note's alternative clause names PERCENT SIGN specifically, not cl-13 as a class — the scoping this case's own rationale states in full.

cases.quote: EN: There is an alternative way to give a third order opportunity for inter-character spacing expansion, to take up to a maximum of a quarter em space, with respect to the corresponding character size, between a preceding grouped numeral (cl-24) and a trailing Western character (cl-27). — JA: 前に配置する連数字中の文字（cl-24）と後ろに配置する欧文用文字（cl-27）との字間で優先順位が第3段階の最大で四分アキまで文字サイズ比で均等に空ける処理は可とする方法もある．
cases.rationale:
Table 6's own `(24, 27)` cell states `limit: None`, `residual: false`, citing this note (`crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table6.rs`): the captured table's own default reading at this coordinate is no opportunity, confirmed directly against the capture file's own reconciliation note (`spec/captured/table6.en.tsv`: 'note 11 -- on a *white* cell -- offers "an alternative way to give a fourth order opportunity" only as a deviation from the table's own default reading of "blank"' — the identical structure this coordinate shares with note 11's own, a note offering an alternative to a captured blank cell). §E.2 note 9's own text records that alternative concretely: a third order (stage 3) opportunity up to a quarter em, the identical ceiling and stage §E.2 note 10 states at a different coordinate (`(27, 13)`, this file's own `E.2/western-character-then-postfixed-abbreviation/the-general-rule-opens-a-third-stage-quarter-em` case) — but unlike note 10, which `evaluate.rs`'s own `note_governed_expansion` reads through a caller-declared condition, no policy question in `spec/derived/questions.tsv` is addressed to `E.2#9` at all (checked directly: no row's `address` column reads `E.2#9`), and `Question::GROUPED_NUMERAL_BEFORE_WESTERN` — §C.2#10's own breakability question over the identical class pair — answers nothing about expansion (`docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s own `E.2#9` entry states the same absence). This case consequently publishes the one reading this workspace can construct, `standing: "normative"`: no opportunity, citing the note that states it. The note's own alternative ceiling is not a reading the published format cannot represent — `E.2/western-character-then-postfixed-abbreviation/the-general-rule-opens-a-third-stage-quarter-em` is proof it can, at a sibling coordinate — it is a reading this project's policy space leaves an unfilled slot for, in exactly the sense `crates/jlreq-line/src/lib.rs`'s own "Wired, not slotted" / "Slots" sections state for a design choice JLReq leaves open: this project never silently guesses at one, and a policy question over this exact class pair is the concrete change a later round would make to give this second reading a policy-selectable home.

The fixture reuses the leading half-em `5` `A.13/grouped-numeral-percent/line-break` and this file's own `E.2/grouped-numeral-percent/the-main-clause-denies-expansion` both use for cl-24, and pairs it with a trailing proportional `A` — the same occurrence `E.2/western-character-then-postfixed-abbreviation/the-general-rule-opens-a-third-stage-quarter-em`'s own `advance: 700, frame: "proportional"` reads for cl-27 — rather than a second European numeral, so the trailing occurrence is unambiguously cl-27 and not itself a candidate for cl-24's own grouping (`docs/decisions/european-numeral-by-code-point.md`). `spaces: []` because Table 1's own `(24, 27)` cell carries no term of either referent's (`terms: &[]`, `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table1.rs`), the identical blank-Table-1 shape this file's cl-08/cl-24 coordinates already read.

permitted.source: JLReq's own captured Table 6, independent of note 9's own unselectable alternative

forbidden.why: §E.2 note 9's own words state this exact ceiling — a third order opportunity up to a quarter em — as its alternative reading, and a justifier who reads only the note's own sentence, without checking Table 6's own captured cell, would publish it as the coordinate's answer. `spec/derived/questions.tsv` names no question addressed to `E.2#9` (checked directly), and Table 6's own `(24, 27)` cell states `limit: None`, `residual: false`, citing this note as the reading its own captured 'blank' cell publishes; asserting the note's alternative as `permitted` would claim a policy this workspace's policy space cannot construct, exactly the unimplemented-alternative failure this suite's `forbidden` array exists to record, and `docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s own `E.2#9` entry names the identical absence as this rule's scope limit.
